sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenSpec is a spec framework for AI coding assistants. Before code is written, your AI drafts a proposal, requirements, a design and a task list as plain Markdown in your repo; you review the plan, then the AI implements it and archives the change.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI coding assistants often start writing code before anyone agrees on what should be built. OpenSpec adds a lightweight planning step with reviewable specs, and keeps those specs up to date as changes are archived.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and 30+ other AI tools
Teams coordinating features across several repos
Anyone wanting reviewable plans before AI writes code
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a fluid, iterative spec workflow built for brownfield code, with plain Markdown specs. Stores for cross-repo planning are still in beta.
requirements: Optional: Node.js 22.20+ for the npm install

overview: After openspec init, you use skills in your AI assistant. /openspec-explore is a thinking partner that reads your code and shapes a plan. /openspec-propose creates a change folder with proposal.md, specs, design.md and tasks.md. /openspec-apply-change implements the tasks, and /openspec-archive-change archives the change and updates the specs.

Specs are plain Markdown with requirements and concrete WHEN and THEN scenarios, so there is no special syntax. OpenSpec is built with OpenSpec, and its own specs and in-flight changes are in the repository as examples.

For teams, Stores (in beta) put planning in a repository of its own so one change can span several code repos and a platform team can own shared requirements. It supports 30+ tools and installs via a script, npm, Homebrew, pnpm, yarn, bun or Nix.

troubleshooting.problem: Slash command doesn't work in Codex
